newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht weak onshore, interbank eases late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht weak onshore, interbank eases late.

text.p: The Thai baht eased to a new record low against the dollar in late trade in the domestic market on strong demand for the dollar by local commercial players, dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 29.10/29.30 to the dollar late in the onshore market compared with 29.05/29.15 in morning trade.
"The baht was traded as low as 29.20 baht today. It's the record low for the baht in onshore market, I've ever seen," said one dealer at a European bank.
The Bank of Thailand set the weighted average interbank exchange rate at 28.922 to the dollar against 28.578 on Monday.
"The trading volume remained thin. Most banks just demanded dollars to cover their clients' positions," the dealer said.
Dealers said local importers and foreign loan borrowers bought dollars to pay for imported goods and repay their loans.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was at 23/28 satangs per dollar late onshore market and 40/50 satangs in the offshore market.
The overnight interbank rate eased to 20-23 percent late from 22-24 percent early morning.
